name: Mintage Pay for WooCommerce
author: mintagepay

sections.description:
Mintage Pay adds card, Cash App and stablecoin checkout to your WooCommerce store. Customers pay by card, Cash App, USDC or USDT. Your share goes straight to your own wallet. Mintage Pay does not hold your sale proceeds.

Built for independent online stores. We review each application.

Three ways to pay

You switch each one on or off and drag them into the order you want.

  • Pay with crypto: the customer pays in USDC or USDT from any wallet or exchange.
  • Pay by card: the customer pays by card (US cards) and you receive USDC. Shown only where Mintage Pay offers card payments for your store.
  • Pay by app: Cash App, where available.

Card and Cash App are not available everywhere. The checkout shows only the options that are open for that order.

Networks

  • USDC on Base, Polygon and Solana.
  • USDT on Polygon, Solana and TRON.

A network shows at checkout only when you have added a payout address for it in your Mintage Pay dashboard.

Get started in minutes

Install the plugin, click “Connect to Mintage Pay” and approve your store. No key to copy. Try it with test money in the free sandbox first, then apply for a live account at https://mintagepay.com/#apply

No monthly fee. Rates are set per store and shown in your dashboard.

How an order works

  1. The customer picks a Mintage Pay method at checkout.
  2. A secure payment window opens over your checkout, so the customer stays on your store.
  3. When the payment is confirmed, Mintage Pay tells your store and the order moves to Processing by itself.

Features

  • Works with the classic checkout and the Cart and Checkout blocks.
  • Compatible with High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS).
  • Signed webhooks. The plugin re-reads the invoice from the Mintage Pay API before it changes an order, so it never trusts a webhook body on its own.
  • Part payments put the order on hold with a note showing what is still owed.
  • A payment whose amount or currency does not match the order puts the order on hold, so you can check before you ship.
  • Unpaid orders are cancelled when the payment window closes, and the stock goes back.
  • An order box on the order screen with the payment status, the payments received and a Refresh link.
  • Payment details on each order: a plain explanation of what happened (paid, incomplete or needs attention), with Paid, Needs attention and Incomplete views of your orders. All Orders stays as it is.
  • Refunds started from the order screen. You send the refund from your own wallet, and the plugin records it on the order.
  • Test mode: a sandbox key connects to the sandbox by itself, and a notice reminds you while it is saved.
  • WooCommerce Subscriptions: each renewal becomes an invoice, and Mintage Pay emails the customer the payment link.
  • USD and 56 other store currencies. Prices in another currency are converted to the USD amount the customer pays in USDC or USDT.
  • One-click automatic updates for the plugin.

Disputes and refunds

Stablecoin payments are final. Card payments follow card network rules, so disputes can happen on card orders. Refunds are your decision.

Other platforms and no-code options

Mintage Pay also has plugins and connections for other store platforms, payment links, a buy button, a REST API and signed webhooks. See https://mintagepay.com/docs/

Get help

  • Docs: https://mintagepay.com/docs/
  • Public group: https://t.me/MintagePayOfficial
  • Email: hello@mintagepay.com (we reply within one business day)

Our team will never message you first, and we never ask for seed phrases, passwords or login codes.

External services

This plugin connects to the Mintage Pay API (https://app.mintagepay.com, or https://sandbox.mintagepay.com for test keys) to take payments. It is the payment service the plugin is for, so it does not work without it.

What is sent, and when:

  • When you click “Connect to Mintage Pay” (or “Connect a test (sandbox) account”): your browser opens app.mintagepay.com (or sandbox.mintagepay.com) with this site’s address, its name, the plugin version, a random value and a code challenge (PKCE). You sign in there and approve this store. Your browser then comes back to this site with a one-time code, and the plugin sends that code and its secret to Mintage Pay to receive this store’s API key. Nothing is sent before you click.
  • When you save the settings, reconnect the webhook, or activate, deactivate or delete the plugin: your API key (in the Authorization header), this store’s webhook URL and the store name, to check the key and to add or remove the webhook endpoint.
  • When a customer chooses Mintage Pay at checkout: the order total and currency, the order number, a description (“Order #1042 from Your Store”), the thank-you and cancel page addresses, the WooCommerce order id and order key, the invoice expiry, and the customer’s billing email address. Mintage Pay emails the customer a receipt only if you turn off “Let WooCommerce send the order emails”; otherwise it writes to them only when they ask for a refund on Mintage Pay’s refund page. For an order paid by card, the email is also kept as part of the record of that card payment, in case the customer disputes the charge.
  • When a customer is sent to the payment page in the whole browser tab (the checkout pop-up is off, “Pay for order”, or the “Complete payment” button): the customer’s billing name, email address, phone number and billing address, and the invoice id, so the card form can be filled in. Mintage Pay hands them out once, to the customer’s own browser, and deletes them at that moment, or within 30 minutes if the customer never opens the payment page.
  • With WooCommerce Subscriptions: the subscription’s recurring total, billing period and the renewal order numbers, the customer’s email address and name so Mintage Pay can send them each renewal’s payment link, and the store language.
  • When an order is updated (a webhook from Mintage Pay, the thank-you page, the order screen, the “Hold stock” timer, or cancelling an order): the Mintage Pay invoice id, to read or cancel that invoice.
  • Merchant payment details: the invoice reference is sent to authenticated read-only diagnostics endpoints. The plugin receives curated codes and explanations, caches them in order metadata, and subscribes its existing webhook endpoint to diagnostics.updated when the server supports it. Background history reads and diagnostic notifications do not change order status, stock, refunds or customer emails. Raw provider payloads and identity-verification inputs are not displayed.
  • With each request the active plugin makes to the Mintage Pay API: the plugin’s name and version in the user agent (for example MintagePay-WooCommerce/1.17.0), so Mintage Pay can see which version of the plugin this store runs.
  • On the checkout page, at most every 12 hours: a request for the list of networks you have turned on, to describe them under the payment method.
  • On the checkout page, for the order total (remembered for 10 minutes per total, 30 minutes for the card form’s address): the total, the currency and this store’s address, to ask Mintage Pay which ways to pay (card, apps, crypto) it offers for that total and in which US states card payments are not available.
  • In the customer’s browser, when the pop-up payment page is closed before paying: the Mintage Pay invoice id and the step the customer was on (for example “choose”), with no cookies, so Mintage Pay can count where buyers stop.
  • Card payments: when the card form is shown inside the checkout (with the pop-up on, where Mintage Pay offers it), that form is Mintage Pay’s own page from app.mintagepay.com. What the customer types there goes to Mintage Pay and the providers it uses for card payments (Stripe and Privy), as described in Mintage Pay’s privacy policy, not to this store.

Mintage Pay terms of service: https://mintagepay.com/terms.html
Mintage Pay privacy policy: https://mintagepay.com/privacy.html
sections.installation:
1. Install. In WordPress go to Plugins > Add New Plugin, search for “Mintage Pay”, click Install Now, then Activate. WooCommerce must be active.

2. Try it with test money (free, no review). Create a test account at https://sandbox.mintagepay.com and add a payout address. Guide: https://mintagepay.com/docs/sandbox/

3. Connect your store. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Payments > Mintage Pay and click “Connect to Mintage Pay” (or “Connect a test (sandbox) account”). Sign in to Mintage Pay, check that the store address shown is yours, and click Approve. You come back to WordPress with the key saved, the webhook registered and the payment method switched on.

Prefer to paste a key? In the Mintage Pay dashboard go to Developers > API keys and create one, paste it in the plugin settings, tick Enable and save.

4. Go live. Apply at https://mintagepay.com/#apply. Once your account is approved, sign in at https://app.mintagepay.com, add a payout address for each network you want to be paid on, then click “Connect to Mintage Pay” again to switch from the sandbox to your live account. The plugin asks before it replaces a working key.

5. Choose your methods. Under WooCommerce > Settings > Payments, switch on “Mintage Pay: Pay by card” and “Mintage Pay: Pay with crypto” if you want them as their own methods, and drag the methods into the order you want.

6. Stay up to date. Tick “Update Mintage Pay automatically” on the settings page, or click “Enable auto-updates” next to Mintage Pay on the Plugins screen.

Full guide: https://mintagepay.com/docs/integrations/woocommerce/
sections.faq:
Do I need a Mintage Pay account?

Yes. A sandbox account for testing is free and instant at https://sandbox.mintagepay.com. A live account is by application at https://mintagepay.com/#apply. We review each application.

What can my customers pay with?

Card (US cards), Cash App, USDC or USDT. Card and Cash App are not available everywhere, and the checkout shows only the options that are open for that order. USDC works on Base, Polygon and Solana. USDT works on Polygon, Solana and TRON.

Does Mintage Pay hold my money?

No. Mintage Pay does not hold your sale proceeds. Your share goes straight to your own wallet, to the payout address you set for each network.

What does it cost?

Rates are set per store and shown in your dashboard. No monthly fee.

What about disputes and refunds?

Stablecoin payments are final. Card payments follow card network rules, so disputes can happen on card orders. Refunds are your decision. Because the money is in your own wallet, you send a refund from your wallet. Click “Refund via Mintage Pay” on the order screen, follow the “Send now” link in the order notes, and the plugin records the refund on the order and WooCommerce emails the customer.

Can I try it before I go live?

Yes. Connect a sandbox account from the plugin settings and place a test order with free test money. Nothing real moves in the sandbox.

What does “Connect to Mintage Pay” do?

It makes an API key for this store in your Mintage Pay account and saves it here, so you never copy a key by hand. You approve it on Mintage Pay’s own site, signed in to your account, and the page shows the store address that asked. Only approve if you just clicked Connect in your own WordPress. The key appears under Developers > API keys as “WooCommerce (your store address)” and the account owner gets an email. If you connect the same store again, the key from the earlier Connect is revoked as soon as the new one is used. Keys you made by hand are never touched.

Why don’t I see Pay by card or Pay by app?

Card and app payments are turned on for each store, and they are not available everywhere. If your live account does not show them yet, email hello@mintagepay.com.

Which store currencies work?

US dollars and 56 other currencies. Crypto payments are in US dollar stablecoins, so a price in another currency is converted at checkout and the payment page shows both amounts.

Does it work with the block checkout and HPOS?

Yes. It works with the classic checkout, the Cart and Checkout blocks and High-Performance Order Storage.

What happens if a customer closes the payment window?

The order stays Pending payment until the payment window ends (60 minutes by default, and you can change it). Then the order is cancelled and the stock goes back. If the customer comes back to the thank-you page first, the plugin checks the payment itself and updates the order.
sections.changelog:
1.24.1

  • Fix: saving payment details on an order no longer marks the order as modified or sends WooCommerce “order updated” events on stores that use High-Performance Order Storage. On HPOS stores running WooCommerce 8.1 to 8.7, payment details stay off until WooCommerce is updated.
  • Fix: a store whose Mintage Pay webhook is not set up checks again every 15 minutes instead of every minute.
  • Fix: an order whose payment details cannot be loaded no longer shows “updating” forever.
  • Fix: two translator notes added for Plugin Check.

1.24.0

  • Added merchant payment diagnostics: curated reason codes, explanations, evidence source and recent history in the order screen and list.
  • Added focused Paid, Needs attention and Incomplete views for Mintage Pay orders. All Orders and normal WooCommerce payment states remain available.
  • Added isolated background diagnostic refresh, signed notification opt-in, and resumable history discovery across the retained 180-day activity window and existing local orders.
  • Older servers remain compatible. Unavailable or incomplete history is shown explicitly. Diagnostic refreshes do not send customer emails or change payments, stock, refunds or order status.
  • New expiry notes explain that an unpaid payment window ending does not establish a card decline.

1.23.0

  • New: a customer who comes back to the cart or checkout with an unpaid Mintage Pay order from the last hour sees a notice, “You have an unfinished payment for order #N. Finish payment”. The link reuses the same invoice and their saved details; no new order is made.
  • Changed: the card method’s checkout text now says where the card form really opens (a window on the page, or the payment page after the order is placed), and no longer says “debit or credit”, because Mintage Pay decides per store which cards it takes.
  • Changed: the “Pay by card” choice no longer disappears when Mintage Pay is slow or briefly unreachable. The last good answer for the same order total is used for up to 24 hours. A store that never had a good answer still hides it.
  • Changed: the customer’s billing state is now sent as the 2-letter code the card form uses (“Calif.”, “New York” and “N.Y.” work; military and territory codes are left for the customer to pick). When the billing address is empty the shipping address is used, and a phone number is sent only when it has 10 or more digits.
  • Changed: the Back button while the payment pop-up is open now asks to leave, like the Close button, instead of leaving the checkout.

1.22.3

  • New: when a customer goes to the payment page in the whole tab (the pop-up is off, “Pay for order”, or the “Complete payment” button on the thank-you page), their billing details now fill in the card form, as they already did in the pop-up. The store hands Mintage Pay the details and gets back a single-use code that is valid for 15 minutes; the code travels in the part of the address after “#”, which browsers never send to any server. If anything goes wrong, the customer simply goes to the payment page as before.
  • New: “Complete payment” on the thank-you page now goes through your store, which makes the code when the button is clicked (at most 5 times per order in 10 minutes).
  • Changed: the reminder email links to your store’s “pay for order” page instead of the payment page.
  • Changed: WooCommerce’s “Pay” and “Cancel” buttons no longer show in My account > Orders for orders waiting on a Mintage Pay payment, so a customer cannot open a second invoice or cancel an order that may be paid.
  • Changed: with “Pay by card” and “Pay by app” in one method, a billing state the card route does not serve (New York, Hawaii) now has “Pay by app” already selected.
  • Changed: a customer who typed their full name in the first-name box now gets both names in the card form.
  • Changed: clearer wording when the pop-up asks to leave, and when a payment could not be started.
  • Fix: a pop-up that fell back to the full page is now counted in Mintage Pay’s checkout funnel.

1.22.2

  • Fix: on stores whose order-numbering add-on assigns the order number a moment after checkout, unpaid orders now show the store’s order number in Mintage Pay too, not only paid ones. The plugin checks the number again about 90 seconds after checkout (and once more 10 minutes later if it was not assigned yet), and also labels an earlier unpaid invoice of the same order with that number.

1.22.1

  • Fix: a payment made on an earlier Mintage Pay invoice is no longer lost when the customer retries checkout. This happened on stores whose order-numbering add-on renames the order after the first try: the retry opened a second invoice, the paid one was ignored, and the order could end up Cancelled. Now a retry goes back to the invoice that already has money on it, and a paid earlier invoice becomes the order’s invoice and marks the order paid.
  • Fix: a second invoice that closes unpaid no longer cancels an order when an earlier invoice for it received money. The order gets a note to review instead.

1.22.0

  • New: Mintage Pay now records your store’s order number when it is assigned after checkout, so the number in your Mintage Pay dashboard matches the one in WooCommerce.
  • Changed: Card method: stores that use the standard “Pay by Debit Card” wording now show “Pay by Card”, since credit cards are accepted. The old standard description (“Debit card, in a secure window on this page. Credit cards will not work.”) now reads “Debit or credit card, in a secure window on this page.” Wording you wrote yourself is not touched, and nothing is saved or rewritten on upgrade.

1.21.0

  • New: “Refund via Mintage Pay” on the order screen creates the refund in Mintage Pay for you to send from your wallet. The order notes get a “Send now” link, and the Mintage Pay box on the order lists refunds waiting to be sent. Nothing moves until you send it: then the refund is added to the order, the items are restocked if you ticked “Restock”, and the customer gets the refund email. Clicking twice makes one refund.
  • New: when Mintage Pay needs the customer’s refund address first, the order note links to the payment, where you ask the customer for it.
  • New: a “Return my funds” page on your store for customers who paid by card in the payment pop-up. Mintage Pay’s emails link to it. It is never cached or indexed.
  • Note: a refund asked for through the WooCommerce REST API on a Mintage Pay order also creates the refund in Mintage Pay, and the API answers with an error because nothing has been sent yet.
  • Where your Mintage Pay account cannot create refunds from the store yet, the button works as before.

1.20.0

  • Change: where “Pay by card” is its own method, the “Pay by app” text now says what buyers pay with: “Cash App in one tap”, plus crypto, Apple Pay and Google Pay where Mintage Pay offers them for the cart. Before, it listed stablecoin networks. A description you wrote yourself is kept.

1.19.0

  • Better: the card form in the payment pop-up is filled in from the order’s billing details whatever the buyer picked at checkout, also when they move from “Pay by app” to a card.
  • Change: “Pay by app” shows the Apple Pay and Google Pay icons, and names them, only where Mintage Pay offers them for the store. Where it does not, the method shows Cash App (and crypto, unless “Pay with crypto” is its own method).

1.18.0

  • New: “Connect to Mintage Pay”. Click it on the settings page, sign in to Mintage Pay and approve your store: the API key is saved, the webhook is registered and the payment method is switched on. No key to copy. “Connect a test (sandbox) account” does the same with test money. If a working key is already saved, the plugin asks before replacing it.
  • New: a “Get started” box on the settings page while no key is saved, with Connect, the sandbox, the application form and the setup guide.
  • New: “Update Mintage Pay automatically” on the settings page (WordPress’s own auto-update setting for this plugin).
  • WooCommerce’s Payments page now shows the Mintage Pay icon, says the method needs setup until a key is verified and shows test mode for a sandbox key, and links to the guide, pricing and terms. Each Mintage Pay method opens its own settings.
  • Fix: with only the main method on, its row showed the Cash App, Apple Pay and Google Pay icons even where Mintage Pay does not offer those apps for the store. The icons now follow what Mintage Pay offers, on the classic and the block checkout.
  • Tested with WooCommerce 11.2.

1.17.0

  • New payment method “Mintage Pay: Pay with crypto”: crypto as its own method at checkout, with USDC, USDT and wallet icons. It opens the payment page straight on the list of networks. Switch it on under WooCommerce > Settings > Payments and drag the methods into the order you want (for example: Pay by card, Pay by app, Pay with crypto). It uses the main Mintage Pay method’s settings (API key, pop-up, expiry, emails), and the USDC / USDT discount applies to it too. Off by default.
  • While “Pay with crypto” is on, the main method is the apps: Cash App in one tap, plus Apple Pay and Google Pay where Mintage Pay offers them for the total. Its row shows those icons, and its payment page no longer offers crypto inside it.
  • Pay by app now shows Cash App, Apple Pay and Google Pay icons. Venmo, PayPal and Coinbase are no longer offered on it.
  • New: when the store paid an app’s fee (for example Cash App one-tap’s), the order note says how much came out of your payout. The amount received is that much less than the order total; it is not an underpayment.

1.16.0

  • Pay by card is hidden for a billing address in a US state where Stripe’s card payments are not available (today New York). Mintage Pay sends the list, so it can change without a plugin update. The classic checkout and the blocks checkout both check it as the customer fills in the address.
  • The apartment or suite line of the billing address is now sent to the card form on its own, not joined onto the street line. Stripe refused some addresses with the two joined.
  • Card on checkout fills the apartment line too.

1.15.0

  • Refund requests as order notes: when a customer asks you for a refund on the Mintage Pay refund page, the order gets a note with the amount, the reason and their message, and another when you approve or decline it, when the customer withdraws it, or when it is waiting for you again because its refund was cancelled. You answer in your Mintage Pay dashboard (Refunds); the customer is emailed your answer. The order’s status is never changed: an approved refund is added to the order once Mintage Pay records it (sent from your wallet or your exchange).
  • Orders paid in crypto: the processing, completed and invoice emails now say where the customer can ask you for a refund (card orders already did).
  • The webhook now also receives refund request events. A store connected with an earlier version is updated once, from an admin page, keeping every event it already receives. An older Mintage Pay server that does not know these events is asked again the next day; invoice and dispute events keep working meanwhile.

1.14.1

  • Stores that pay every card fee themselves (set by Mintage Pay support): the card buyer now pays the order total only. Both the Mintage Pay service fee and Stripe’s card fee come out of the store’s payout. The checkout text, the “Pay by card or Pay by app” choice, the statement note, the thank-you page and the order emails say so and mention no fees.
  • New: on such a card order, the order note says how much of Stripe’s card fee was paid from your payout (the amount received is that much less than the order total; it is not an underpayment).

1.14.0

  • Card on checkout: with “Mintage Pay: Pay by card” on, the classic checkout shows the card form itself. It fills from the billing fields, asks for Stripe Link’s code when needed, and saves the card when the customer clicks Place order (nothing is charged yet). The pop-up on the new order then charges that card straight away when the total is within the “at most” shown. A wallet that already holds enough pays the order without a new card charge, and a declined card is never picked again on its own.
  • Card orders in customer emails: the processing, completed, invoice and refunded emails of an order paid by card now show the card charge, the name on the card statement (once Mintage Pay sets it), that a bank may hold up to about 3% more for a short time, and a link where the customer can ask you for a refund. The refunded email also tells the customer the refund settles any dispute they opened with their bank. Printed once per email, and only for orders that were paid by card.
  • Card disputes as order notes: when a customer disputes a card charge (reported by you in the Mintage Pay dashboard or API, by the customer, or by Mintage Pay), the order gets a note, and another each time the dispute changes. The order’s status is never changed.
  • The webhook now also receives card dispute events. A store connected with an earlier version is updated once, from an admin page, keeping every event it already receives. An older Mintage Pay server that does not know these events is asked again the next day, and invoice events keep working meanwhile.
  • The customer’s billing email is now always passed to Mintage Pay with the order. With “Customer emails” on (the default) Mintage Pay still sends no receipt and no refund email; it writes to the customer only when they ask for a refund themselves. The email lets a card customer find their order on the refund page, and is part of the record a card dispute needs.

1.13.2

  • New: “Card statement note” on the Pay by card method, on by default. It tells card buyers what their bank or card statement will show (STRIPE*PRIVY, INC., not your store name), so the charge does not alarm them: under “Pay by card” at checkout, on the thank-you page and in the customer’s order emails, for card orders only. Switch it off or write your own text under WooCommerce > Settings > Payments > Mintage Pay: Pay by card.
  • Stores that pay the Mintage Pay service fee on card payments themselves (set by Mintage Pay support): the checkout text, the card form and the statement note no longer mention a service fee; the buyer pays the order total plus the card fee only.

1.13.1

  • Fixed: on themes that make every label inline-block (Bootstrap does), the payment method row with the most icons dropped below its own radio button on a phone. The two Mintage Pay rows now keep the radio and the title on one line and wrap their icons under the title.

1.13.0

  • “Pay by card” can now be its own payment method at checkout, next to the main Mintage Pay method, instead of two choices inside it. Switch on “Mintage Pay: Pay by card” under WooCommerce > Settings > Payments; while it is on, the main method opens the apps (Apple Pay, Google Pay, Cash App, Venmo, PayPal, Coinbase, crypto wallets) and stops showing the two choices. Drag the two methods into the order you want.
  • The card method keeps only its own name, description and on/off switch: the API key, the pop-up, the invoice expiry, reminders and emails all stay on the main method, and there is still one webhook.
  • Subscriptions and the “save when you pay with USDC or USDT” discount stay with the main method: a renewal cannot ask a buyer for a card, and the discount is for paying in stablecoins. The card method is hidden for a cart with a subscription in it.
  • The card method is only shown when Mintage Pay really takes a card for the order’s total (Stripe will not take less than $1.00, fees included).
  • Each of the two methods carries its own brand icons on its row at checkout (Visa and Mastercard; Apple Pay, Google Pay, Cash App, Venmo, PayPal, Coinbase and wallets), where the choice inside the method used to carry them.

1.12.1

  • Fixed: on themes that restyle every radio button in the payment box, “Pay by card” and “Pay by app” could be unreadable (the radio filled the row and the text wrapped one letter per line). The two rows now keep the browser’s own 16px radio, their layout and their icons whatever the theme does.

1.12.0

  • “Pay by card” and “Pay by app”: when your Mintage Pay account takes card payments, the checkout shows two choices under Mintage Pay, card first, each with its brand icons (Visa and Mastercard; Apple Pay, Google Pay, Cash App, Venmo, PayPal, Coinbase and wallets). “Pay by card” opens the card form directly, with the customer’s billing details already filled in; “Pay by app” opens the list of apps. Without card payments, or for an order below the card minimum, the checkout looks as before. New setting to turn the two choices off (on by default).
  • Payment pop-up on the block checkout too: “Place order” opens the payment over the checkout instead of leaving the store. Closing it keeps the order and shows a notice; “Place order” again reopens the same payment.
  • Payment pop-up: the frame may use the camera (the card form’s ID check) and the payment sheet.
  • Fixed: on the block checkout the pop-up details reached the browser as the word “Array” (with a PHP warning in the log).
  • Log: when Mintage Pay refuses a request, the log line names the fields it objected to (field names only, never values).

1.11.2

  • Block checkout: the “pay with USDC / USDT” discount now reaches the cart through its own Store API update (it was registered too late, so the browser console showed an error on each payment method change).

1.11.1

  • Checkout and thank-you scripts are enqueued (no inline script tags).
  • Configuration warnings show on the Plugins and WooCommerce screens only.

1.11.0

  • New optional setting “Payment reminder (minutes)”: if a customer chose Mintage Pay and the order is still unpaid after that many minutes, they get one email with a link back to their payment. Not sent when the order was paid, changed to another payment method, or the same customer has a newer paid order. The email is a normal WooCommerce email (“Mintage Pay: finish your payment”) you can edit or switch off under WooCommerce > Settings > Emails. Off (0) by default.
  • Payment pop-up: closing it tells Mintage Pay at which step it was closed (an anonymous count in the checkout funnel, nothing about the customer).

1.10.0

  • New optional setting “Payment pop-up”: on the classic checkout, “Place order” opens the Mintage Pay payment page in a pop-up over your checkout, so the customer never leaves your store. When the payment is in, the customer goes straight to your order-received page. Closing the pop-up keeps the order; “Place order” again reopens the same payment. Your Mintage Pay account must be switched on for it; until then, or if the pop-up cannot load, customers are sent to the payment page as before. The block checkout keeps the usual redirect. Off by default.

1.9.0

  • 36 more store currencies: NGN, ARS, PHP, IDR, VND, PKR, EGP, BDT, KES, GHS, TZS, COP, CLP, PEN, UYU, PYG, BOB, DOP, GTQ, CRC, THB, MYR, TWD, LKR, NPR, KZT, UAH, ILS, SAR, QAR, CZK, HUF, RON, ISK, XAF and XOF (57 in all). VND, CLP, PYG, ISK, XAF and XOF have no decimals.

1.8.0

  • New optional setting “Discount for paying with Mintage Pay (%)”: card payments cost you about 3% and Mintage Pay costs less, so you can pass part of the saving on. The checkout says “Save 3% when you pay with USDC or USDT.” and, while the customer has Mintage Pay selected, a “Discount for paying with USDC / USDT” line comes off the products (after coupons, before shipping). Works with the classic and the block checkout. Off (0) by default.

1.7.0

  • Renamed to Mintage Pay. API keys now start with mp_live_ / mp_test_ and webhooks are signed in the MintagePay-Signature header. The plugin’s name changed with it, so this is a fresh install: remove the earlier plugin and connect this one with a new API key.

1.6.0

  • Test keys (mp_test_…) now connect to the Mintage Pay sandbox automatically. “API base URL” is empty by default and only needed for a development server. A key used with the wrong host says so (“This looks like a test key; …”).
  • The settings page shows which Mintage Pay account the store is connected to and whether it is live or in test mode, and an admin notice shows while a test key is saved.
  • Refunds: “Refund via Mintage Pay” no longer leaves you with only “Refund manually”. It explains that refunds are sent from your Mintage Pay dashboard and links there, and refunds nothing. A refund entered by hand in WooCommerce no longer emails the customer “Refunded” before money has moved; the real Mintage Pay refund is matched to it when it is confirmed, so the two are never counted twice.
  • The checkout description lists only the networks you have turned on (or says “Pay with USDC or USDT from your crypto wallet or exchange.” until Mintage Pay reports them). A description you wrote yourself is kept.
  • The thank-you page for an order that is not paid yet says “Waiting for your payment” with a “Complete payment” button, instead of “Your order has been received”.
  • Order notes show amounts to the cent (the exact amounts stay in the order data), one payment per line, with the full transaction hash linked to the block explorer.
  • New setting “Customer emails” (on by default): WooCommerce sends the order emails and Mintage Pay sends no separate receipt.
  • Tested with WordPress 7.1.

1.5.0

  • WooCommerce Subscriptions support. Each renewal becomes a Mintage Pay invoice and the customer gets the payment link by email. An unpaid renewal is marked Failed. Cancelling a subscription cancels it at Mintage Pay.
  • Webhook events other than invoice events (for example subscription events) are accepted and ignored.

1.4.0

  • Orders paid a little short (within your Mintage Pay underpayment tolerance) complete with a note showing the shortfall.
  • Payments held for a sanctions review stay pending until cleared.

1.3.0

  • Prices in EUR, GBP, CAD, AUD, JPY and more. Stores in a supported currency send the price in that currency; Mintage Pay converts it to the USD amount the customer pays, and the order notes show the rate. A paid invoice completes the order only when its price matches the order total in the store currency.
  • Refunds on orders in a currency other than USD are noted on the order for you to record by hand, since the refund is sent in USD.

1.2.0

  • Bank transfer (ACH or wire) for stores approved for it: when the customer chooses it on the payment page, the order goes On hold with the bank reference (so it is not cancelled as an abandoned checkout), and the customer’s email and thank-you page explain how to finish paying. When you record the money in your Mintage Pay dashboard, the order moves to Processing. If the payment window passes with nothing paid, the order is cancelled.

1.1.0

  • Refunds recorded in the Mintage Pay dashboard (verified on the blockchain) now appear on the WooCommerce order as refund records, once each, never more than what is still refundable. Stock and the gateway are not touched.

1.0.1

  • The “Hold stock” timer no longer cancels an order whose invoice has money on it: the invoice is checked with Mintage Pay first, and if Mintage Pay cannot be reached the order is checked again on the next run.
  • Cancelling an order now cancels its open or partially paid Mintage Pay invoice.
  • A paid invoice is only completed when its amount and currency match the order total; otherwise the order goes on hold with a note.
  • An invoice that closes part paid puts the order on hold with a note to refund or collect the rest, instead of cancelling it.
  • A late partial payment on a cancelled order keeps the order cancelled and adds a note to refund the customer.
  • A retry no longer sends the customer to an invoice that is about to expire.
  • The payment method is only offered once the API key has been verified. An admin notice shows when it is not.
  • Changing the API key now also removes the old webhook endpoint for this store, even when the old key was already revoked.
  • Deactivating the plugin disables the store’s webhook endpoint.
  • No more “Overpaid” note for amounts under one cent (the TRON unique-amount offset).
  • The thank-you page only asks for the rest of a partial payment while the invoice can still be paid.

1.0.0

  • First release.

short_description: Take card, Cash App, USDC and USDT payments in WooCommerce. Your share goes straight to your own wallet.
description:
Mintage Pay adds card, Cash App and stablecoin checkout to your WooCommerce store. Customers pay by card, Cash App, USDC or USDT. Your share goes straight to your own wallet. Mintage Pay does not hold your sale proceeds.

Built for independent online stores. We review each application.

Three ways to pay

You switch each one on or off and drag them into the order you want.

  • Pay with crypto: the customer pays in USDC or USDT from any wallet or exchange.
  • Pay by card: the customer pays by card (US cards) and you receive USDC. Shown only where Mintage Pay offers card payments for your store.
  • Pay by app: Cash App, where available.

Card and Cash App are not available everywhere. The checkout shows only the options that are open for that order.

Networks

  • USDC on Base, Polygon and Solana.
  • USDT on Polygon, Solana and TRON.

A network shows at checkout only when you have added a payout address for it in your Mintage Pay dashboard.

Get started in minutes

Install the plugin, click “Connect to Mintage Pay” and approve your store. No key to copy. Try it with test money in the free sandbox first, then apply for a live account at https://mintagepay.com/#apply

No monthly fee. Rates are set per store and shown in your dashboard.

How an order works

  1. The customer picks a Mintage Pay method at checkout.
  2. A secure payment window opens over your checkout, so the customer stays on your store.
  3. When the payment is confirmed, Mintage Pay tells your store and the order moves to Processing by itself.

Features

  • Works with the classic checkout and the Cart and Checkout blocks.
  • Compatible with High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS).
  • Signed webhooks. The plugin re-reads the invoice from the Mintage Pay API before it changes an order, so it never trusts a webhook body on its own.
  • Part payments put the order on hold with a note showing what is still owed.
  • A payment whose amount or currency does not match the order puts the order on hold, so you can check before you ship.
  • Unpaid orders are cancelled when the payment window closes, and the stock goes back.
  • An order box on the order screen with the payment status, the payments received and a Refresh link.
  • Payment details on each order: a plain explanation of what happened (paid, incomplete or needs attention), with Paid, Needs attention and Incomplete views of your orders. All Orders stays as it is.
  • Refunds started from the order screen. You send the refund from your own wallet, and the plugin records it on the order.
  • Test mode: a sandbox key connects to the sandbox by itself, and a notice reminds you while it is saved.
  • WooCommerce Subscriptions: each renewal becomes an invoice, and Mintage Pay emails the customer the payment link.
  • USD and 56 other store currencies. Prices in another currency are converted to the USD amount the customer pays in USDC or USDT.
  • One-click automatic updates for the plugin.

Disputes and refunds

Stablecoin payments are final. Card payments follow card network rules, so disputes can happen on card orders. Refunds are your decision.

Other platforms and no-code options

Mintage Pay also has plugins and connections for other store platforms, payment links, a buy button, a REST API and signed webhooks. See https://mintagepay.com/docs/

Get help

  • Docs: https://mintagepay.com/docs/
  • Public group: https://t.me/MintagePayOfficial
  • Email: hello@mintagepay.com (we reply within one business day)

Our team will never message you first, and we never ask for seed phrases, passwords or login codes.

External services

This plugin connects to the Mintage Pay API (https://app.mintagepay.com, or https://sandbox.mintagepay.com for test keys) to take payments. It is the payment service the plugin is for, so it does not work without it.

What is sent, and when:

  • When you click “Connect to Mintage Pay” (or “Connect a test (sandbox) account”): your browser opens app.mintagepay.com (or sandbox.mintagepay.com) with this site’s address, its name, the plugin version, a random value and a code challenge (PKCE). You sign in there and approve this store. Your browser then comes back to this site with a one-time code, and the plugin sends that code and its secret to Mintage Pay to receive this store’s API key. Nothing is sent before you click.
  • When you save the settings, reconnect the webhook, or activate, deactivate or delete the plugin: your API key (in the Authorization header), this store’s webhook URL and the store name, to check the key and to add or remove the webhook endpoint.
  • When a customer chooses Mintage Pay at checkout: the order total and currency, the order number, a description (“Order #1042 from Your Store”), the thank-you and cancel page addresses, the WooCommerce order id and order key, the invoice expiry, and the customer’s billing email address. Mintage Pay emails the customer a receipt only if you turn off “Let WooCommerce send the order emails”; otherwise it writes to them only when they ask for a refund on Mintage Pay’s refund page. For an order paid by card, the email is also kept as part of the record of that card payment, in case the customer disputes the charge.
  • When a customer is sent to the payment page in the whole browser tab (the checkout pop-up is off, “Pay for order”, or the “Complete payment” button): the customer’s billing name, email address, phone number and billing address, and the invoice id, so the card form can be filled in. Mintage Pay hands them out once, to the customer’s own browser, and deletes them at that moment, or within 30 minutes if the customer never opens the payment page.
  • With WooCommerce Subscriptions: the subscription’s recurring total, billing period and the renewal order numbers, the customer’s email address and name so Mintage Pay can send them each renewal’s payment link, and the store language.
  • When an order is updated (a webhook from Mintage Pay, the thank-you page, the order screen, the “Hold stock” timer, or cancelling an order): the Mintage Pay invoice id, to read or cancel that invoice.
  • Merchant payment details: the invoice reference is sent to authenticated read-only diagnostics endpoints. The plugin receives curated codes and explanations, caches them in order metadata, and subscribes its existing webhook endpoint to diagnostics.updated when the server supports it. Background history reads and diagnostic notifications do not change order status, stock, refunds or customer emails. Raw provider payloads and identity-verification inputs are not displayed.
  • With each request the active plugin makes to the Mintage Pay API: the plugin’s name and version in the user agent (for example MintagePay-WooCommerce/1.17.0), so Mintage Pay can see which version of the plugin this store runs.
  • On the checkout page, at most every 12 hours: a request for the list of networks you have turned on, to describe them under the payment method.
  • On the checkout page, for the order total (remembered for 10 minutes per total, 30 minutes for the card form’s address): the total, the currency and this store’s address, to ask Mintage Pay which ways to pay (card, apps, crypto) it offers for that total and in which US states card payments are not available.
  • In the customer’s browser, when the pop-up payment page is closed before paying: the Mintage Pay invoice id and the step the customer was on (for example “choose”), with no cookies, so Mintage Pay can count where buyers stop.
  • Card payments: when the card form is shown inside the checkout (with the pop-up on, where Mintage Pay offers it), that form is Mintage Pay’s own page from app.mintagepay.com. What the customer types there goes to Mintage Pay and the providers it uses for card payments (Stripe and Privy), as described in Mintage Pay’s privacy policy, not to this store.

Mintage Pay terms of service: https://mintagepay.com/terms.html
Mintage Pay privacy policy: https://mintagepay.com/privacy.html

upgrade_notice.1.24.1: Safety fix for 1.24.0: payment details no longer mark orders as modified on HPOS stores. Recommended for every store.
upgrade_notice.1.24.0: Adds payment explanations and focused order views, with background loading of retained history. All Orders and payment processing are unchanged. Requires a diagnostics-enabled Mintage Pay server for the new details.
upgrade_notice.1.23.0: Clearer card wording, a steadier Pay by card choice and a Finish payment notice for customers who return. Recommended for every store.
upgrade_notice.1.22.3: Full-page card payments now arrive with the customer's billing details filled in. Recommended for every store.
upgrade_notice.1.22.1: Fixes paid orders showing Cancelled after a checkout retry on stores that rename orders after checkout. Recommended for every store.
upgrade_notice.1.22.0: The card method now shows "Pay by Card" instead of "Pay by Debit Card", since credit cards are accepted. Your own wording is not changed.
upgrade_notice.1.21.0: "Refund via Mintage Pay" now creates the refund in Mintage Pay, with a Send now link in the order notes. The order, stock and customer email follow once you send it. Adds a Return my funds page for card buyers.
upgrade_notice.1.20.0: "Pay by app" says Cash App in one tap at checkout instead of listing stablecoin networks. Your own description is kept.
upgrade_notice.1.19.0: The card form in the payment pop-up is filled in from the billing details for every payment choice, so buyers type less. Apple Pay and Google Pay are shown only where Mintage Pay offers them.
upgrade_notice.1.18.0: One-click "Connect to Mintage Pay" (no key to copy), a Get started box, an "Update Mintage Pay automatically" setting, and a fix for app icons shown where the apps are not offered.
